title: Automated Expunge Engine and Evidence Bundles for Geo-Scoped Residency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an "Expunge Engine" that automates the end-to-end right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF) flow for customers with geo-scoped residency and configurable retention rules. The engine must coordinate deletion across Redwood hosting tiers (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC), create tamper-evident evidence bundles, and provide machine- and human-readable verification artifacts for auditors.

Objectives: 
- Allow customers to define retention and residency policies per-tenant, per-region, and per-storage-class via Console + API.
- Implement an automated deletion pipeline that guarantees percent-complete deletion across data planes and surfaces a proof-of-removal artifact.
- Produce signed evidence bundles that include manifests, checksums, deletion logs, and KMS-backed signatures.
- Provide a verification API and downloadable evidence package (JSONL + SHA256 manifest + signature) for customer audits and regulator requests.

Scope: 
- Policy authoring UX (Console + API) for retention windows and residency constraints. 
- Backend expunge coordinator that enqueues deletion work, supports dry-run, canary mode, and final commit. 
- Deletion connectors for object stores, trace & logs, embeddings indexers, and model KV caches. 
- Evidence generation: manifest, per-entity deletion receipts, signed transaction log, TTL proofs, and compact audit summaries. 
- Webhooks and dashboard signals for completion/failure and automated attestations export.

Out of scope for MVP: cross-account federation, long-term evidence archival UI (we will provide download/export only).
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create retention + residency policies via Console and API and assign them to tenant scopes.
Expunge Engine runs a dry-run & canary deletion and reports expected vs. actual deletes in the Console for a sample dataset.
Evidence bundle is produced for completed deletions: includes manifest, per-entity receipts, SHA256 checksums, and a KMS-signed envelope.
Verification API returns a signed statement that can be validated by the customer's KMS public key and includes deletion timestamps and data-plane confirmations.
Automated telemetry: success/failure rates, per-region latency, and a retry/backoff strategy are instrumented and visible in Console charts.
End-to-end tests + integration tests exist for Hosted/Dedicated/Private flows and pass in CI.
Operational runbook created with rollback steps and customer-facing incident guidance.
